docs.title: mkdocs-metadata-enricher-plugin
docs.text: Enrich your MkDocs sitemap and search index with real git revision dates.

docs.title: What does this plugin do?
docs.text:
Out-of-the-box, MkDocs generates sitemaps and search indexes with build-time dates — not the dates your pages were actually last updated. This is suboptimal for:

  • SEO — search engines prefer pages with accurate <lastmod> timestamps
  • User experience — readers want to know when documentation was actually changed
  • Search results — the built-in search index doesn't show any update information

mkdocs-metadata-enricher-plugin fixes this by:

  1. Extracting the actual last commit date for each page from git history
  2. Injecting it into sitemap.xml as proper <lastmod> entries
  3. Adding formatted dates to search index entries so users see when content was last updated

See it in action

Try the search on this site — each result shows a last-updated date pulled from git history. You can also inspect the sitemap.xml to see <lastmod> dates.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Description 🔄 Sitemap enrichment Adds git revision dates to <lastmod> tags in sitemap.xml 🔍 Search enrichment Shows formatted git dates in search results 📅 Flexible formatting date, datetime, iso_date, iso_datetime, or custom strftime 🌍 Timezone & locale Display dates in any timezone and language 🎯 Theme agnostic Works with Material, ReadTheDocs, or any MkDocs theme ⚡ Independent formatting Search dates are formatted independently from page display dates

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: All configuration options for mkdocs-metadata-enricher-plugin live under the metadata-enricher key in your mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Basic Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description enrich_sitemap bool true Add git dates to <lastmod> tags in sitemap.xml enrich_search bool true Add formatted dates to search index entries

docs.title: Search Index Date Formatting
docs.text:
These options control how dates appear in search results when enrich_search: true.

Option Type Default Description search_date_type str iso_date Date format (see below) search_custom_format str %d. %B %Y Python strftime format (only used when search_date_type: custom) search_timezone str UTC IANA timezone for date display search_locale str en Locale code for date localization

docs.title: iso_date (default)
docs.text: 2025-04-27

docs.title: date
docs.text:
With search_locale: en:

April 27, 2025

With search_locale: de:

27. April 2025

docs.title: datetime
docs.text:
With search_locale: en:

April 27, 2025 13:11:28

docs.title: custom
docs.text:
Use any Python strftime format string:

search_date_type: custom
search_custom_format: "%d/%m/%Y"

Result:

27/04/2025

docs.title: Full Example
docs.text:
site_name: My Documentation
docs_dir: docs
site_dir: site

plugins:
  - search

  - git-revision-date-localized:
      type: date
      timezone: Europe/Amsterdam
      locale: en

  - metadata-enricher:
      enrich_sitemap: true
      enrich_search: true
      search_date_type: datetime
      search_timezone: Europe/Amsterdam
      search_locale: en
      search_custom_format: "%d. %B %Y"  # Only used if search_date_type: custom

docs.title: Minimal Example
docs.text:
If you only want sitemap enrichment and are happy with ISO date format in search:

plugins:
  - search
  - git-revision-date-localized
  - metadata-enricher

All defaults will apply: enrich_sitemap: true, enrich_search: true, search_date_type: iso_date, search_timezone: UTC, search_locale: en.

docs.title: Plugin ordering
docs.text:
Plugin order matters

git-revision-date-localized must appear before metadata-enricher in your plugin list. The metadata enricher reads the git dates that the revision date plugin sets on each page's metadata.

docs.title: Development Guide
docs.text: This guide will help you set up a development environment and contribute to the mkdocs-metadata-enricher-plugin project.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.9 or later
  • uv package manager (install via curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh)
  • Git (for version control and testing)
  • pre-commit (installed via dev dependencies)

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/cms-cat/mkdocs-metadata-enricher-plugin.git
cd mkdocs-metadata-enricher-plugin

docs.title: 2. Initialize the Development Environment
docs.text:
# Install development dependencies
uv sync --all-extras

# Initialize pre-commit hooks (prek is a drop-in replacement for pre-commit)
prek install
# Or if you prefer the traditional pre-commit:
# pre-commit install

docs.title: 3. Verify Setup
docs.text:
# Run tests
uv run pytest

# Run linting
uv run ruff check .

# Run formatting check
uv run ruff format --check .

# Run all pre-commit/prek checks
prek run --all-files
# Or with traditional pre-commit:

docs.title: Code Style
docs.text:
The project uses ruff for linting and formatting. All code is automatically formatted using:

uv run ruff format .

And checked with:

uv run ruff check . --fix

These are also run automatically via pre-commit hooks when you commit.

docs.title: Writing Code
docs.text:
• Use type hints for all function parameters and return values
  • Write docstrings using Google style format
  • Keep functions focused and well-documented
  • Follow PEP 8 conventions

Example:

def _format_date(self, dt: datetime, fmt: str) -> str:
    """
    Format a datetime object.

    Args:
        dt: The datetime to format.
        fmt: The format string to use.

    Returns:
        The formatted date string.
    """
    return dt.strftime(fmt)

docs.title: Adding Tests
docs.text:
All new features should include tests. Tests go in the tests/ directory and follow naming convention test_*.py.

Unit tests (in test_plugin.py): - Test individual functions and methods in isolation - Use mocking for external dependencies (git, filesystem) - Mark with @pytest.mark.unit

Integration tests (in test_integration.py): - Test with actual MkDocs builds - Verify end-to-end behavior - Mark with @pytest.mark.integration

Run tests with:

# All tests
uv run pytest

# Only unit tests
uv run pytest -m unit

# Only integration tests
uv run pytest -m integration

# With coverage report
uv run pytest --cov=src/mkdocs_metadata_enricher_plugin

docs.title: Publishing to PyPI
docs.text:
Publishing is handled by GitHub Actions using trusted publishing (OIDC). To release:

  1. Update version in src/mkdocs_metadata_enricher_plugin/__init__.py: 

    __version__ = "0.2.0"

  2. Update CHANGELOG.md with release notes

  3. Commit and tag: 

    git add .
git commit -m "Release version 0.2.0"
git tag v0.2.0
git push origin main v0.2.0

  4. GitHub Actions automatically:

  5. Builds the package
  6. Runs tests
  7. Publishes to PyPI

Note: First-time setup requires configuring PyPI trusted publishers: - Go to PyPI project settings - Add a trusted publisher for the GitHub repo with environment name pypi

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Install and configure mkdocs-metadata-enricher-plugin in under 2 minutes.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pipuv 
pip install mkdocs-metadata-enricher-plugin

uv add mkdocs-metadata-enricher-plugin

This will also install the required dependency mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Add the plugin to your mkdocs.yml. The order matters — the git revision date plugin must run before the metadata enricher:

plugins:
  - search

  # Must run BEFORE metadata-enricher to provide git data
  - git-revision-date-localized:
      type: date
      enable_creation_date: false

  # Enriches sitemap & search index with git dates
  - metadata-enricher:
      enrich_sitemap: true
      enrich_search: true
      search_date_type: datetime
      search_locale: en

docs.title: Build your docs
docs.text:
mkdocs build

That's it! Your sitemap.xml will now contain accurate <lastmod> dates and your search index will show when each page was last updated.

docs.title: Verify it works
docs.text: After building, you can inspect the results:

docs.title: Sitemap
docs.text:
Open site/sitemap.xml and look for <lastmod> entries:

<url>
  <loc>https://example.com/my-page/</loc>
  <lastmod>2025-11-03</lastmod>
</url>

docs.title: Search index
docs.text:
Open site/search/search_index.json and look for dates in the text field of each entry. With search_date_type: datetime, you'll see something like:

{
  "location": "my-page/",
  "title": "My Page",
  "text": "April 27, 2025 13:11:28 — Page content here..."
}

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: This page explains the enrichment pipeline and shows before/after comparisons.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
When MkDocs builds your site, it generates two important files:

  • sitemap.xml — used by search engines to discover and index your pages
  • search/search_index.json — used by the built-in search to find content

By default, neither of these files contains accurate revision dates. The sitemap may use the build date, and the search index contains no date information at all.

docs.title: The Solution
docs.text:
The plugin hooks into two MkDocs build events:

graph LR
    A[MkDocs Build] --> B[on_page_context]
    B --> C[Cache git dates per page]
    A --> D[on_post_build]
    D --> E[Enrich sitemap.xml]
    D --> F[Enrich search_index.json]

docs.title: Step 1: Collect git dates (on_page_context)
docs.text: During the build, the plugin reads the git revision date that git-revision-date-localized-plugin has already extracted and cached for each page. It stores this date in an internal cache keyed by page path.

docs.title: Step 2: Enrich sitemap (on_post_build)
docs.text: After the build completes, the plugin reads the generated sitemap.xml and replaces or adds <lastmod> entries with the actual git commit dates.

docs.title: Step 3: Enrich search index (on_post_build)
docs.text: The plugin reads search/search_index.json and prepends a formatted date string to the text field of each search entry. This makes the date visible in search results.

docs.title: Sitemap
docs.text:
Before (default MkDocs output):

<url>
  <loc>https://example.com/getting-started/</loc>
  <!-- No <lastmod> or uses build date -->
</url>

After (with metadata-enricher):

<url>
  <loc>https://example.com/getting-started/</loc>
  <lastmod>2025-11-03</lastmod>
</url>

docs.title: Search Index
docs.text:
Before (default MkDocs output):

{
  "location": "getting-started/",
  "title": "Getting Started",
  "text": "Install and configure the plugin..."
}

After (with search_date_type: datetime, search_locale: en):

{
  "location": "getting-started/",
  "title": "Getting Started",
  "text": "November 3, 2025 14:22:05 — Install and configure the plugin..."
}

The date appears as a prefix in the search text, making it visible when users search your documentation.

docs.title: Integration with git-revision-date-localized
docs.text:
This plugin does not read git history itself during the page-rendering phase. Instead, it relies on mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin to extract and set revision dates in each page's metadata. The metadata enricher then reads these cached dates and uses them for sitemap and search enrichment.

For the search index fallback path (cache misses), the plugin queries git directly using:

git log -1 --format=%aI -- <filepath>

This returns the author date of the last commit that touched the file, in ISO 8601 format.

docs.title: SEO Benefits
docs.text:
Search engines like Google use <lastmod> in sitemaps to:

  • Prioritise crawling recently updated pages
  • Display "last updated" dates in search results
  • Assess content freshness

By providing accurate git-based dates instead of build dates, your documentation appears more trustworthy and up-to-date to search engines.
